transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-20

- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel, Jordan Lee (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Marcus Duval, Aisha Rahman (Silverpine)

Auto-generated Summary (may be noisy):
Redwood did a hosted API demo showing embeddings + rerank. Customer asked about latency and cost, data residency, and SSO. SE showed console, demoed sample search, and explained caching and batching. Next steps include pilot and benchmark.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, this is jordan our se, and we'll walk through a short hosted api demo focused on embeddings and the rerank endpoint. how's everyone doing?
00:12 Lena: good thanks, excited to see this. we, um, frankly have been tweaking our current algolia pipeline but hit issues on complex relevance across product attributes.
00:25 Marcus: yeah our main ask is: better semantic recall plus reranking for recency and business rules, but cost is a constraint.
00:32 Aisha: timeline is Q1 pilot, production in Q2 if it looks good. security is a hard requirement - SOC2 and SSO.
00:44 Jordan: great, we'll try to cover those. quick agenda: 1) hosted embeddings endpoint and vector store pattern, 2) reranker endpoint and how it integrates with your candidate set, 3) console and optimize hints for cost/latency, and 4) next steps/pilot.
01:04 Maya: i'll start with a high level: redwood's hosted api gives you a single call to embed text and a separate rerank rpc that takes a query and N candidates and returns a score and optional explanation. it's built to be low-latency and supports streaming for long outputs but for our rerank flow you usually use sync response.
01:28 Lena: quick q — vector dims. we use 1536 in house, does redwood support that?
01:36 Jordan: yes, we host open model catalogs — 1536 dims common; also 1024/768 depending on model. backend is optimized for cosine or l2. slight note: the encoder model choice affects runtime, e.g., smaller encoders mean cheaper per-embed.
01:53 Marcus: can you talk about indexing? we currently use faiss on-prem.
02:00 Jordan: sure, for hosted we usually export dense vectors to your vector DB (faiss/pinecone/vespa/algolia hybrid) but we also offer rerank where you send candidate doc ids + embeddings or we call back to your vector DB. many customers keep faiss for offline indexing and use our rerank just for the final scoring to control ordering with business rules.
02:25 Maya: i'll share the architecture diagram after this — link in the notes: https://redwood.ai/deck/search-demo (shared)
02:34 Lena: perfect.
02:40 Jordan: demo time — i'll switch to console. (brief screen share noises)
02:45 Jordan: here in the console you pick model, then embedding config, then deploy. we're showing two models: an efficient embedder (fast, 8-15ms/embed) and a high-quality one (35-60ms/embed). for rerank we default to a reranker that's optimized for short candidate lists — 10 to 50 candidates — and we support batching for larger fanout.
03:13 Marcus: those numbers — are they p99 or median?
03:18 Jordan: medians in hosted region us-west-2; p95 about 1.5x median. so the 8-15ms is median for small text. rerank median for 10 candidates was ~80ms in our test corpus; p95 closer to 180ms depending on model complexity.
03:35 Aisha: and cost per query?
03:38 Jordan: depends on tokens, embedding model, and whether you push candidates pre-filtered. rough thumb: embedding call per doc ~ $0.0005 for efficient model, rerank call for 10 candidates ~ $0.003-$0.01 depending on model choice and token counts. we can run a tailored cost calc for your query distribution.
04:02 Lena: that's helpful. also, how do you handle caching? our hot docs are queried a lot.
04:08 Jordan: we have prefix and kv caching — mis-transcripted sometimes as K-V cash in notes — so common prefixes and cached vectors reduce calls. caching is pluggable; you can use our runtime caching or an external redis layer.
04:22 Maya: also redwood optimize will analyze your traffic and suggest batching sizes and quantization for embeddings; often suggestion: use 8-bit quantized encoder for bulk indexing then full-precision for live rerank.
04:35 Marcus: quantization for embeddings — any quality loss?
04:38 Jordan: minimal for coarse recall, more noticeable for fine-grain re-rank unless you retrain or calibrate. Optimize provides A/B suggestion with eval score deltas, we can show expected nDCG lift/loss.
04:55 Lena: security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS. can hosted meet that?
05:03 Maya: yes. hosted api supports SAML SSO for console access, role-based access control, and detailed audit logs. for key management we integrate with major KMS systems; for strict KMS customers we recommend private deployment, but we do offer encrypted-at-rest and will work with you on contractual requirements.
05:23 Aisha: what about data residency? we're EU customers for half our users.
05:27 Jordan: we have regions in eu-central-1 and can pin workloads. we also support private (VPC) deployments for stricter residency. note — some smaller features like early-batch caching may be region-limited depending on hardware.
05:45 Marcus: ok demo — can we run a quick live rerank with our sample?
05:50 Maya: we brought a canned example with sample product snippets. jordan will call the hosted rerank with a query and 12 candidate docs.
06:02 Jordan: (typing) initiating rerank call...
06:08 System: request sent
06:12 Jordan: results back — shows top-3 reorder and explanation tokens for each score. you'll see the reranker boosts recency when business rule tag present, we can toggle that in payload.
06:25 Lena: looks promising, can we feed business rules via metadata?
06:29 Jordan: yes you pass a metadata blob per candidate and we can surface feature weights. sample payload docs: {id, embedding, metadata:{is_promoted:true, recency_days:3}} — (note: transcript sometimes garbles braces).
06:46 Marcus: any multi-language support? we have a large FR and ES catalog.
06:50 Jordan: yes, multilingual embedders available, quality varies by language. we recommend language-specific encoders if you need high fidelity.
06:58 Lena: what's the recommended flow for low-latency storefront search? we need sub-200ms end-to-end.
07:05 Jordan: typical pattern: 1) ANN candidate recall (faiss/pinecone) 2) fetch top 100 vectors/doc snippets (you can prefetch embeddings cached), 3) call rerank with top 10-20 candidates. that keeps rerank cost and latency down; e2e under 200ms is achievable with tuning and region placement.
07:28 Maya: and Optimize will recommend batching and cache TTLs to hit your SLAs while controlling cost.
07:35 Aisha: ok got it. can you show where we change model rollouts?
07:41 Jordan: console -> models -> rollout. you can canary to 10% traffic, compare latency/perf in app traces, then promote. we have built-in eval hooks so you can tie rollouts to nDCG on your test set.
07:58 Marcus: about metrics — can we see token-level cost and per-route breakdown?
08:02 Maya: yep console has token/call cost breakdown and per-model latency histograms, also traces you can export to your observability stack.
08:14 Lena: question on vendor lock — if we decide to move off hosted, can we export models/configs?
08:19 Jordan: yes configs and model artifacts are exportable; we give model weights pointers and config manifests. we also provide terraform modules for private deploy.
08:30 Aisha: thx. any limitations on candidate size for rerank? we may sometimes have 200 candidates pre-filtered before scoring.
08:37 Jordan: rerank is optimized for small lists; for 200 we'd advise a two-stage rerank or chunked batching. the cost and latency scales roughly linearly with candidate count, so we recommend candidate prefilter and then rerank top subset.
08:52 Lena: can we log decisions for audit? we need to be able to reproduce ranking for specific queries.
:08:57 Jordan: yes, audit logs capture input payload and deterministic seed for rerank; you can replay locally to reproduce.
09:08 Maya: quick pause — any red flags?
09:11 Aisha: just contractual SLAs and KMS, otherwise looks good.
09:15 Lena: i'd like to try a small pilot on product search for 6 weeks.
09:20 Maya: perfect. pilot plan: we'll set up hosted test tenant, ingest 100k docs, run two embedding models and rerank config A/B, 1-week perf sweep, then a 3-week online pilot with your live traffic sampling.
09:36 Marcus: data handoff — we'll put sample on S3 and share link with jordan.
09:40 Jordan: noted — please make sure the docs have doc_id and minimal metadata; we use that for traces.
09:46 Maya: i'll follow up with pricing tiers and the starter pilot SOW.
09:51 Aisha: what's the expected cost for pilot?
09:53 Maya: ballpark $5-8k for a 6-week pilot depending on embed/rerank model; we'll confirm in proposal.
09:59 Jordan: one more note on costs: you can save using quantized vectors for indexing and only use higher-precision models for rerank. Optimize will give expected savings.
10:14 Lena: ok let's talk procurement cycles — we have legal review that takes ~2 weeks.
10:19 Maya: good to know; we'll time the pilot to start once that clears.
10:23 Jordan: i'll also attach a small benchmark spreadsheet with our test traces: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/silverpine-sample.csv
10:32 Marcus: great.
10:35 Maya: wrapping up — recap: send pilot SOW and pricing (maya), run hosted rerank perf (jordan), silverpine to send sample data and labels (marcus).
10:48 Aisha: agreed. any risks?
10:50 Jordan: potential perf tuning needed for non-english heavy workloads; will surface in benchmarks.
10:56 Lena: thanks everyone.
11:00 Meeting end.
